story_moved_reason: Marginal but real movement, not a big jump: Ibu's overnight ash column rose to 600m (from the 400m baseline in the Sept-14 draft) across three fresh eruptions into early Sept 15; Ili Lewotolok logged a new Sept 15 06:32 WITA eruption explicitly flagged 'still in progress' by PVMBG; Semeru posted a fresh 1,000m column again at 04:32 WIB Sept 15, extending its streak to a second consecutive day. Nothing has changed at the alert-level layer -- the same 5 volcanoes (Anak Krakatau, Semeru, Lewotobi Laki-laki, Sinabung, Merapi) remain at Level III (Siaga), so the 'three more volcanoes' framing in the working title is NOT a new development, it's a recap of the unchanged Sept-14 list. The missing-boat/Arupadhatu 1 search (5 journalists + 3 crew, Sunda Strait) has posted NO update since day 6 (Sept 13: 15 vessels + 1 helicopter, 300 personnel, 8 missing) in any outlet checked -- it appears to have dropped off Antara, Detik and Basarnas' own homepage entirely, displaced by the much larger, unrelated Virgo Transport 8 ferry disaster (140 missing in the Java Sea) that has dominated Indonesian SAR coverage since Sept 13.
as_of_line: Fact desk as of 2026-09-15 (fetch time, WIB/WITA/WIT). Sept 14 evening through Sept 15 early-morning items are fresh; the Level III/Siaga volcano list, Sinabung's Aug 31 level change, and the missing-boat day-6 figures are unchanged holdovers and marked [background] or [stalled].

facts.fact: Mount Ibu erupted three more times overnight, each stronger than the Sept 14 midday baseline: 21:45 WIT (600m ash, 1,925masl), 22:08 WIT (400m), 23:44 WIT (400m), and 00:46 WIT Sept 15 (600m ash, 1,925masl) -- all gray ash drifting northeast. Remains Level II (Waspada).
Ibu's Sept 14 21:45-Sept 15 00:46 eruptions recorded seismograph amplitudes of 28mm with durations of 30-47 seconds, reported by observer Darsono Haji Muhammad Nur.

Semeru erupted again at 04:32 WIB Sept 15, ash column 1,000m above the peak (4,676masl) drifting southwest -- matching its Sept 14 peak -- then again at 05:27 WIB with an 800m column (4,476masl) drifting east/southeast, seismograph amplitude 23mm, duration 142-161 seconds. Two additional no-visual eruptions were recorded overnight at 00:10 and 01:23 WIB. Remains Level III (Siaga).
facts.number: 1,000m ash column (matches Sept 14 peak, one more day of continuous activity)

facts.fact: Darwin VAAC / MAGMA's own VONA aviation-color feed confirms Semeru held Orange aviation color code through at least 2026-09-14 22:27 UTC (05:27 WIB Sept 15 local), the same eruption as above -- ash-cloud top estimated 14,323ft (4,476m asl), gray, thick intensity, moving east-southeast.

Ili Lewotolok erupted at 06:32 WITA Sept 15, ash column approx. 100m above the peak (1,523masl), white-to-gray, moderate intensity drifting northwest. PVMBG's report explicitly states the eruption 'was still ongoing' ('erupsi masih berlangsung') at the time of filing -- the freshest live-eruption status of any of the three volcanoes checked. A prior no-visual eruption was also logged at 20:41 WITA Sept 14.
facts.source_name: MAGMA Indonesia (PVMBG/Badan Geologi eruption bulletin), reporter Syawaludin, A.Md.
facts.number: 100m ash column, eruption flagged still in progress

facts.fact: PVMBG's live activity-level table (fetched today) confirms Level III (Siaga) status for exactly 5 volcanoes nationwide: Anak Krakatau (Lampung), Lewotobi Laki-laki (NTT), Merapi (DI Yogyakarta/Jawa Tengah), Semeru (Jawa Timur) and Sinabung (Sumatera Utara). This is UNCHANGED from the Sept-14 draft's list -- no volcano has been added to or removed from Level III since then.

[BACKGROUND, unchanged] Level II (Waspada) count stands at 22 volcanoes nationwide (including Ibu and Ili Lewotolok); Level I (Normal) at 42; Level IV (Awas) at 0. No volcano nationwide is currently at the highest alert tier.

[STALLED -- no update found] The last confirmed status on the missing speedboat Arupadhatu 1 (5 journalists + 3 crew, lost contact in the Sunda Strait en route to Anak Krakatau on Sept 7) is day 6 of the search (Sunday Sept 13): 15 vessels plus 1 helicopter, ~300 personnel, an 8-vessel sub-team sweeping Sector X (681 sq nautical miles) within a 6,024 sq nautical mile total search area. No Antara, Detik, or Basarnas item dated Sept 14-16 mentions the search at all.
facts.number: Day 6, 15 vessels + 1 helicopter, 300 personnel (last known figure; no fresher number located)

facts.fact: [CONTEXT] Basarnas' and Antara's/Detik's SAR coverage since Sept 13 has been almost entirely displaced by an unrelated, much larger incident: the KM Virgo Transport 8 ferry accident in the Java Sea, which has left 6 dead and up to 140 missing as of Sept 13-15, with recovery/underwater operations ongoing through Sept 15. This is the likely reason no fresh Arupadhatu 1 coverage was found.
facts.number: 140 missing (unrelated incident, explains the coverage gap)

facts.fact: [BACKGROUND, unchanged since Aug 31] Sinabung remains at Level III (Siaga), raised from Level II on Aug 31 after a 3,500m ash column; no PVMBG statement found confirming or withdrawing the Aug 31 warning of a possible larger eruption.
facts.source_name: MAGMA Indonesia activity-level page (cross-checked against Sept-14 draft, SudutPandang.id)

unknowns: No day-7/day-8/day-9 update on the Arupadhatu 1 search was found in Antara, Detik, Jakarta Post, or Basarnas' own site as of the fetch -- cannot confirm whether the search was extended, scaled back, or produced any find since day 6 (Sept 13).

The team lead's brief cited 'day 7 of the search, 18 vessels' and '8 airports closed, ~3,000 flights, PVMBG's 3 Sept statement, tiltmeter rising since August' as already-shipped facts from a 15 Sept video, but no local file in ops/wave2 (or elsewhere searched in this worktree) contains those specific figures -- could not cross-check or extend them from source.
Jakarta Post's search page loads results via client-side Google Custom Search JS; curl could not retrieve any article list from it.
VolcanoDiscovery's krakatau/news.html is behind a JS wait-challenge (Akamai/Cloudflare-style) that curl cannot pass; no data retrieved from that source.
Darwin VAAC's bom.gov.au graphics page is also JS-rendered (Akamai bot mitigation); no text advisory content could be extracted via curl.

Could not verify whether Lewotobi Laki-laki or Merapi's Level III status changed in the last 48h (both appear as unchanged holdovers from the Sept-14 draft); no volcano-specific news article confirming a fresh status statement was found for either in this pass.
PVMBG has not, in any source checked, explicitly stated why Ibu's ash column rose from 400m (Sept 14) to 600m (Sept 15 overnight) -- no causal statement, just successive bulletins.
